defect.evidence_quote: society is prepared to recognize as 'reasonable.'
defect.problem: The black-letter rule is broader than the disclosed support. The quoted Katz/Greenwood formulation is not character-faithful to the disclosed pinpoints, and the unlawful-stop/tainted-abandonment clause has no disclosed supporting case record or opinion text.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove quotation marks or use the disclosed Katz wording, and add disclosed authority/text for the unlawful-stop voluntariness rule. Otherwise narrow the rule to the abandoned-property contexts supported by Greenwood, Hester, Abel, Rakas, and Rawlings.

reasons: Katz pin-361 uses the formulation that society is prepared to recognize the expectation as reasonable, not the page's quoted phrase that society accepts it as objectively reasonable.
Greenwood pin-40 is marked slip-only/mismatch and does not contain the quoted standard; Greenwood pin-40b only supports the curbside-trash accessibility rationale.
No disclosed text file or lake record supports the final sentence that contraband dropped only because of an unlawful stop or seizure is not valid abandonment.
residual_risks: Parts of the rule are supported by disclosed records, but the assertion as written cannot be verified from the disclosed universe.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split the rule: keep the expectation-of-privacy/property-law point with Katz/Rakas/Rawlings support, and separately cite a disclosed authority for tainted or involuntary abandonment.
